title: 'J. W. Wellington' to 'José González' (Félix Díaz), n.d. [1922?] (catalogue 1445, CEHM-Carso DCXXI.6.588.1): the 60 cipher runs of folios 2-3 not printed by Narváez, read in part with his key 313

documents.shelfmark: CEHM-Carso, Fondo DCXXI Archivo de Félix Díaz, DCXXI.6.588.1
documents.route: 'J. W. Wellington' (a felicista agent of the Puebla junta) -> 'José González', New Orleans (Félix Díaz's cover name in this fondo)

places.from: probably Puebla (the junta named in the letter)

plaintext.source: Two words in ink over two runs of folio 2 ('Contingentes', 'Republica') and one pencil word in the margin of folio 2 ('Inminencia', the decipherment of run f2.12). No other decipherment. Narváez (2019, p. 369) prints his decipherment of folio 2 paragraphs 2-3 and names folio 1's two runs.

transcription.notes: Folio 2 clear; folio 3 faint (pale typing, watermark over the right margin, ink loops of the signature), read on contrast-stretched crops. Pass 1 and a blind pass 2 by separate AI agents: folio 2 agrees on every letter; folio 3 differs at about ten signs, each settled in NOTES.md (Transcription doubts). A blind pass 3 by two further AI agents agrees except at six signs already marked doubtful.

system.summary: Gronsfeld-type shift over the 27-letter Spanish alphabet (A-N, Ñ, O-Z) with the key 313 (cipher = plain +3, +1, +3, repeating), the cycle starting at the first letter of each run and running on through it; spaces dropped inside a run; runs typed in capitals inside clear Spanish.
system.notes: Key published by Narváez (2019, pp. 367-368; 2015, pp. 126-127). Typing slips: about a dozen single wrong letters, one swap, and a few runs where the cycle is lost.

prior_solution.where: Narváez 2015 pp. 126-127 and 2019 pp. 364-369: key, folio 1's two runs (printed as 'Juárez Escalante'; the cipher gives Suárez), folio 2 paragraphs 2-3; he says the rest decode with 313 and prints none of it.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling set the task and the rules (plan frozen before decoding, blind second transcription, strict counting); AI agents transcribed, decoded, read and counted. No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (decryption, random-key control, word count)
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), viewing the images; a second instance for the blind transcription

solution.what: Narváez 2019 pp. 364-369 read from photographs of the book: key 313, fig. 6 (folio 2), decipherment of folio 2 paragraphs 2-3 printed, the rest left to the reader. Repository checked: no target, PR or issue on DCXXI.6.588.1 (PR #512 is the Sánchez letter).
Five images fetched from visor.cehm.org.mx (plain http, one at a time, no login).
60 runs (folio 2 paragraphs 4-7, all of folio 3) transcribed by one agent, then blind by a second agent from its own crops; disagreements on folio 3 only, settled on the image (NOTES.md).
Plan frozen before decoding (SHA-256 e02991a7...): key 313 unchanged, cycle per run, 1,000 random 3-digit keys as controls. Run once.

Final transcription, fixed decoder: key 313 scores -2.469 (Spanish bigrams); it ties only with 3-1-3 itself drawn among the 1,000 random keys; best other key 3-1-7 at -3.626; controls' mean -5.353 (control_313.txt). Plan, hash, script and output were written within nine seconds, so the plan's priority rests on our word; the key and rule are Narváez's published ones.

Runs divided into words in their clear sentences, every departure marked; scripts/count_words.py checks the marks against the decryption: 247 clean words of an estimated 296 word places (0.834); 250 (0.845) after the third transcription below.

Independent review by a separate AI agent of ours (Claude Opus 5.5, 23 Nov 2026, 00:35-00:55 EST; a model check, not a person's): blind transcription of three runs (folios 1-3) and blind decoding agree letter for letter; it found the decoder skipped unsure signs without advancing the key (fixed: f2.19's last 17 letters became a hole), that folio 1's run reads SUAREZ (Narváez prints Juárez), and readings of slipped runs with a shifted cycle (reported post hoc, not counted).

POST HOC, not counted: one shift of the 3-1-3 cycle per run reads f3.10 (las personas que integran nuestra junta), f3.13 (war names J. Siliceo, F. Sánchez, Miguel Altamirano, Luis Mora; 'F. Sánchez' is the signature of sanchez1922) and part of f3.20.

Third transcription of all 60 runs, blind (two separate AI agents from their own crops, measuring the typewriter pitch): it agrees with the transcription letter for letter except at six signs already marked doubtful (f2.19 s20, f3.04 s5, f3.07 s13-16, f3.10 s42, f3.12 s110, f3.14 s151). It agrees with pass 1 where pass 2 differed in EN (f3.07) and DOCUMENTOS, TESORERO (f3.12), which become clean (250 clean words); it agrees on every sign of the one-letter slips and of the stretches that give no words, which supports their being slips of the typist or encipherer rather than misreadings (model readers, Claude Opus 5.5, about 10:00-10:50 EST; no person has checked).

POST HOC, not counted: every shift of the cycle found so far puts the start of the 3-1-3 cycle on the first letter of a word (f2.19 PAULATINAS, f3.10 DE LAS PERSONAS, f3.20 BONILLA), as the Sánchez letter does at every word, or continues the previous run across a colon (f3.13 after f3.12's 130 letters). A rule frozen on this (plan SHA-256 c17933f5...; scripts/restart_test.py, restart_test.txt) found nothing new: the stretches it had not seen (f3.07 tail, 8 letters; f3.22 tail, 4) are too short to beat shuffled controls, and f3.20's end reads COMO VOCAL EN LA PROPIA JUNTA only with a one-place skip inside PROPIA, outside the rule (the script's mark is met only because its word list splits PRORIA), so it is not counted as a pass. Outside support: the CEHM catalogue names JOSÉ SILICEO and RICARDO LOBATO in a later Wellington letter (DCXXI.6.624.1) and gives J. W. Wellington as a pseudonym of Fidencio E. López (DCXXI.8.731.1).

validation.notes: A Gronsfeld-type key is not a letter-to-value table; the key is published (Narváez) and applied unchanged under a frozen plan, with a random-key control.

outcome.method_basis: Narváez's published key 313 for this letter (2015 pp. 126-127; 2019 pp. 364-369), applied unchanged to the runs he did not print; this completes his reading.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 250 clean words of an estimated 296 word places in the 60 runs (scripts/count_words.py): each unread stretch's words estimated from its letters (5.38 letters per clean word); 275 places, 0.909, if each stretch counts as one word. A word with any repaired, supplied or doubtful letter is a hole.

texts.label: 'J. W. Wellington' to 'José González', n.d.: 60 cipher runs of folios 2-3
texts.summary: A felicista agent reports to Félix Díaz: fear of discouragement for lack of a united force; General Mallén, serving Obregón, has turned Torruco against Cástulo Pérez; Federico Córdoba falsely claims to act for Peláez and Díaz; a movement is ready throughout the state; the Puebla junta's officers and members are named (Lic. José María Camacho, president; Fidencio E. López; Miguel Márquez Galindo; Dr. Alberto Moreno; Machorro, Alvarado, Osorio, García, Pomposo Bonilla); Lic. Ricardo Suárez Escalante (not 'Juárez' as printed by Narváez) is to be called 'Ricardo Lobato'.
texts.note: 250 clean words of an estimated 296 word places in the 60 runs (holes: 11 one-letter slips, 'que es', 'ultimas', 'tenemos' chosen with the decode, 'parecer' with an overtyped sign, 4 unidentified words: 20 hole words; and 5 stretches with no words). Further runs read only post hoc with a restart of the key cycle (NOTES.md), not counted. Narváez's printed part is not counted. Correction: folio 1's run decodes SUAREZ ESCALANTE, not 'Juárez' as Narváez prints.

gaps.detail: Under the watermark and an overtyping.

gaps.item: f2.19 after DESINTEGRACIONES (21 letters), f3.10 after 'LOS NOMBRES' (36), f3.13 the war names (41), f3.20 after 'POMPOSO' (44)
gaps.detail: Slips in the key cycle, read post hoc (pa{N/U}latinas orientación, with one wrong letter; de las personas que integran nuestra junta; J. Siliceo, F. Sánchez, Miguel Altamirano y Luis Mora; Bonilla, hermano del Lic., como vocal en la propia junta, with a second skip inside PROPIA), with the CEHM catalogue naming José Siliceo. Not counted: too little unseen text to test the restart rule frozen afterwards (NOTES.md).

Its fifth sign is S and B typed over each other; S gives PARECER, B nothing, so it is settled only by the decode. (EN, DOCUMENTOS, TESORERO were settled by a third, blind transcription on 23 Nov 2026.)
No human check; a better image or the original would settle them.
